elements.element: No "sole supplier"/sole-and-exclusive provider obligation binding Customer
elements.evidence: "Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term."

elements.element: No other exclusivity or requirements-style commitment binding Customer elsewhere in the clause
elements.evidence: "No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies... its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall."

elements.element: Exclusivity limited to a defined product category
elements.evidence: "hosted analytics services" (category defined, though exclusivity itself removed)

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels
elements.evidence: No service-level trigger appears in revised 2.2

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet delivery dates
elements.evidence: No delivery-date trigger appears in revised 2.2

reasons: The single replacement converts the sole-and-exclusive commitment into a non-exclusive one, so no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer — the preferred (locked) level is fully met.
Change is a short in-place phrase substitution; no fallback mechanics, boilerplate, or unrelated terms were added, and Section 2.1's no-commitment language is untouched.
Fallback elements (12-month cap, automatic SLA/delivery-date termination) are absent, but that is irrelevant since the preferred level is achieved and the two levels are not combined.
No undefined terms, contradictions, or dangling mechanics introduced; 2.2 now reads consistently with 2.1.
